Press Release:


REDISA
You pay R2.30 per kilogram for every new tyre you buy. But is the money being used to create jobs and develop a recycling industry? In an exclusive expose Carte Blanche follows the money and the tyres across South Africa.

Script:


REDISA Final Script Saturday 14th November 2015

Commentary one
On the 1st of August this fire broke out at a tyre depot in Springs –Its registered to Redisa – the recycling and economic development initiative of South Africa - a tyre recycling plan gazetted by the minister of environment

FLAMES

At a recent Redisa function it was clear the minister is a big fan

Minister Edna Molewa
The fact that so many countries of the world are saying this is an envy, and we are actually pathfinders, an example that has got to lead the world!

Commentary two
You pay Redisa R2 30 per kilogram of every tyre you buy, but you wont see it because the manufacturers and importers have added it into the price. They have no choice but to pay over about R50 million rand per month to Redisa, which is headed by the CEO, Hermann Erdmann

Herman
We collected R600 million
Devi
R600 million
Herman nods

Commentary Three
In 2012 the minister gazetted Redisa to develop an effective tyre recycling industry and create 10 000 jobs over 5 years. She can cancel the plan at any time

Devi
How have you done?
Hermann
If we learned anything at this time its, that we performed even better than the plan was saying

Commentary Four
This interview took place last October. It was the second time we had met Herman Erdman. He is a controversial man in the tyre industry. The first time we met him was at his home in Lonehill In 2012

Devi 2012
Will SA be benefitting will the environment be benefitting will the consumer be benefitting
Hermann
Absolutely! I am saying to the industry come and challenge us – we will not hide anything and they must come to you if I am not doing what we are supposed to
Commentary five
Redisa is supposed to: create small transporters to pick up the tyres from tyre shops, or waste pickers to collect tyres in the environment; they take them to tyre depots. From there the tyres should go to a network of recyclers where they can be transformed to be used in roads, rubber products or oil

LINK
Fast forward to August last year and it seemed the wheels were coming off – sources approached Carte Blanche with allegations that not only was the implementation a mess but money was being squandered too

Commentary Six
They said Herman Erdmann and his directors were profiting from Redisa funds. They had moved into fancy mansions, bought cars for cash and were taking international holidays all courtesy of our tyre tax, meant to create jobs and industries

Shiva Source
Their hearts are not in delivering the objective of saving the environment. I think they’re in it for their own personal gain

Commentary Seven
The sources, too scared to go on camera, claimed that Redisa was little more than a patronage network. Hermann they said has powerful friends.

Devi
Sources are complaining that there is not enough governance, the money goes in and you can do what you want to do with it?
Herman
We are stipulated by the rules of the plan and we have very strict governance rules within Redisa

Commentary eight
We didn’t broadcast this interview until now- more than once the minister told us she was happy with Redisa’s performance. When our sources got cold feet we reluctantly abandoned the story

LINK
Carte Blanche asked for financial documents from the department and Redisa but none were forthcoming – then a few weeks ago a memory stick made its way to our offices

Commentary nine
That led us to Terence Sithole and John Maphanga, two unemployed Mamelodi residents who signed up as waste pickers collecting tyres. They were so successful that Redisa gave them awards earlier this year




Terence Sithole
We actually loved what we were doing and we wanted to show and prove to the government and Redisa that we are willing to work …that is why we took every last cent that we had…

Commentary ten
At R2 -00 per tyre the money was terrible, but motivated by Redisa’s promise that they could form businesses- these waste pickers organised themselves into co -operatives.

Derick Mateyo
The most important thing, which pushed all of us to say, lets go and join Redisa, because looking at the Gazette it shows they are going to promote entrepreneurs and co operatives.

Commentary eleven
But then came the disappointment – they say that no matter how hard they worked the co- operative they had formed, had to share R1500 per month.

Terence Sithole
Actually this thing it came as a shock after we realised that we couldn’t even afford to buy bread

Commentary twelve
This contradicts the ministers instructions to Redisa – she says:
“These jobs are meaningful sustainable jobs as there are opportunities for people to own businesses

John
I’ve recruited 20 people for Redisa but they quit all of them

Commentary thirteen
John Maphanga collected around 11 000 tyres. This achievement earned him an award at a glitzy Sandton event. Leader of Zakele cooperative, Derek Mateyo went on John’s behalf, hoping the 15% bonuses they say they were owed would materialise at the awards

Derick Mateyo shorten
They gave me a trophy. I thought there would be a cheque. He starts to laugh- we looked around, but there was no envelope.

Commentary fifteen
Redisa say they are not aware of the specific allegations and couldn’t respond to the claim. They say the wastepickers well-being is critical to them and that ultimately micro collectors will have the prospect of full participation in the economy. But the ones we spoke to feel they have been used.

Hermann Erdmann is under enormous pressure to fulfil his 10 000 jobs target



Source A INSIDER
Herman depends on the waste pickers to boost the employment figures! He doesn’t REALLY care about the collection of the tyres, in actual fact he wouldn’t mind if they DONT collect ANY tyres but he needs them, because he needs the job figures

Commentary Sixteen
Hermann was overseas when we requested an interview. In writing they say
3023 jobs have been created. Of those 1948 jobs are waste pickers, but our sources say less than 5% are real jobs– just an ID number for the minister and the waste picker gets a card

Devi
Are you suggesting there is fraud?
Source A
I would consider it as fraud, YES! And those guys are earning less than R1500 per month.

Commentary Seventeen
Redisa say that their numbers have been audited by KPMG and received two unqualified audits, but even if the wastepicker job numbers supplied by Redisa are indeed accurate our analysis reveals that over seven months this year, their average pay is just R41 per month.

Meanwhile Redisa has a R76 million surplus in their kitty. And marketing spend is well over R20 million since inception

Terence Sithole with a Redisa magazine
Here am I here! We look very happy, but in our pockets are we happy? Nothing! This is what we hoped for that we hoped for that we will grow.

Commentary eighteen
And the minister has bought the spin, hook, line and sinker

But the minister is convinced that Redisa is delivering!

Minister Edna Molewa
Redisa has done well in ensuring jobs that are created, but also having taken away so many tyres away from the landfills

LINK
The whole point of the plan was to RECYCLE the tyres – but that part of the plan was barely working, tyres were piling up in the depots- Herman had to get rid of the tyres – and quickly

Commentary nineteen
So he turned to the solution favoured least in the plan. Burn the tyres for fuel in cement kilns. But the kilns were scattered all over South Africa, so Redisa spends millions on transport –money they should be spending on developing recyclers

Devi
Is every tyre recycled as we stand right now?
Hermann
It’s processed lets say that- ultimately we would like every tyre recycled not burnt

Commentary Twenty
But then the kilns filled up and could take no more tyres so Redisa
started to export the tyres to India and Dubai -creating jobs overseas instead.

Despite these leaked photos of baled tyres about to be shipped, Redisa say: they are not exporting tyres. REDISA delivers tyres to recyclers for processing and a percentage of shredded tyres are being exported.

So they are exporting tyres!

Source Shiva
They could be burning most of the tyres, they could be exporting a lot, but those are all short-term solutions that can help you get your targets.
Devi
Ok
Shiva
The question from there is are you really creating a sustainable industry in SA and the answer is no

Commentary Twenty- two
Hermann has always maintained that tyre dumps attract mosquitoes, yet documents show Redisa was desperate to get rid of tyres, and approved 7000 tonnes to the Sunderland Shooting range after the range met the formal application requirements. Mosquito heaven- courtesy of Redisa!

Devi
Herman’s job is to collect the tyres that is what we are paying him for
Source A
But also remember the more you collect the more you need to pay out

Commentary Twenty-Three
Two years from now Redisa is mandated to deal with 100% of the tyres. Right now they only need to divert 50% of the tyres from landfills. But why spend millions simply diverting them from one place to another – last October Hermann admitted they had a problem

Hermann
And I tell you why we not collecting all the tyres yet – we don’t know where to put them


Commentary Twenty- four
One year later Redisa appears to have the same problem. These photos taken a few weeks ago show tyres at the Cape Depot piled high against the wall close to a power line. This is a violation of waste tyre storage regulations but Redisa say all their depots are fully compliant and they handled the Springs fire well
Devi
Ok so Herman is collecting the tyre tax levy but he doesn’t want to collect the tyres because what must he do with them?
Source A
It’s definitely not in Redisa’s interest to collect 100% of the tyres at this stage in time

Commentary Twenty- five
Albert Bothma had ticked all the boxes and his 51% BEE company become Redisa’s first approved recycler. Ask him if they have fulfilled their mandate and this is his response

Albert
That is so far from the truth at this point in time!

Commentary Twenty-six
To get the business off the ground all he needed was a guarantee from Redisa for 800 tonnes a month – and international investors would bring R150 million to the party – sulphur free diesel, waxes and electricity would have been made in this abandoned brewery. But he claims Redisa provided no such guarantee

Albert
It destroyed the project in the sense that the financiers said it doesn’t fall in their parameters any more

Commentary Twenty- Seven
Redisa say that Alberts plant is not in operation yet and they have commited to supplying an amount based on his current supply in his area. Albert just laughed when we read him their response.

Redisa also says they are working with 11 new recyclers at various levels of activity

Devi Link
Then Herman went on a shopping Spree and spent millions on machinery, ostensibly to set up a few politically connected people in businesses

Commentary Twenty-eight
Redisa has denied that former special advisor to the minister Star Vilakazi will be a beneficiary of a tyre cutter – even though he has been listed as a beneficiary in this Redisa document. The other beneficiaries also have close political ties

Source A
In order to facilitate businesses for these individuals we were creating a industry that isn’t supposed to be there in between Redisa and the recyclers in other words – we are now putting an extra cost on this whole Redisa process just to help these guys make money


Commentary Twenty-nine
The plan says its crucial to identify likely candidates from MK, the Woman’s league and youth league and its those organisations who identify the individuals who benefit.

Khotatso Moloi; Nafcoc secretary General Gilbert Mosena; Victor Molefe; Bafana Dube, and Tshepo Molai

Devi to Herman
Why did you want to help them?
Herman
It’s in the plan and we don’t do anything that is not in the plan

Commentary thirty
The machines are worth millions and we found them stored across the country.

Victor Molefe is set up with R19.5 million worth of machinery
Bafane Dube gets the R15.5 million moulding plant;
ex MK Khotatso Moloi does well with R26 million rand’s worth of gear and a land cruiser and Gilbert Mosena even better with R29 million rand of equipment. They refused to comment but Tshepo Molai who has been named in the arms deal confirmed that he is negotiating a pre processing facility with Redisa.

Devi
There is no plan in this country where government doesn’t eat a big fat chunk of this how did you do this?
Hermann laughs
I maybe can quote what someone in the department said it was a politician. Redisa would be here, it doesn’t matter if somebody lobbies for it or not because it is the right thing to do

Commentary thirty-one
Small transporter Bongani Mkhabela had no idea that Redisa was looking for entrepreneurs close to the corridors of power –not down in the trenches where he was getting his hands dirty

Bongani
My journey with Redisa is something I would never wish anyone to be in – It’s only bought pain to me, my family and everyone else around me

Commentary thirty-two
He claims that when they took away his profitable route he suggested other opportunities within Redisa. Each time the answer was no – Redisa claims they have engaged Bongani on issues of non collection and there is an on going investigation

Bongani
Basically they shut me out of the business
Devi
What has happened to your truck?
Bongani
I had to sell it
Devi
And your house
I lost my house as well …he breaks down

Devi
Are they happy?
Hermann
We have great feedback, in the beginning I said who are the people we are accountable to and I think it’s the waste pickers, the transporters and the recyclers because we are influencing their livelihood every day and we see them as our customers so we try to treat them like that

Commentary thirty- three
Bongani has no house but Hermann now has a selection. Redisa owns this R18 million rand mansion in Sandton, but this is Hermann’s primary address in Constantia, called Heaven of the Cape. It’s leased to a company- Westfalen owned by his wife and son. Westfalen has paid R1.74 million rand in advance for Hermann to live here.

When we asked Redisa if any funds were paid to Westfalen they said no. But the next day they qualified this, saying that the property is also used for Redisa business and Westfalen does get R15 000 per month in lieue of business expenses

Devi
What would you like to say to people who insist that you are living the high life?
Hermann
I would like to talk about implementing the plan – it was something that we said if you have criticism in things we do come back to practical examples and become part of it

Commentary 34
Well here is one example of many. Why did Redisa spend over R770 000 in a single month - June 2014 on travel and accommodation?

Hermann is also a shareholder of the management company that administers Redisa. Its called Kusaga Taka

Devi
Can we see Redisa’s books, can we see Kusaga Taka books?
Herman
No obviously not,
Why not?
Hermann
Because I don’t think it’s a reasonable request -we can’t go to Goodyear and say can we see your books!

Commentary 35
From March to September over R327 million rand came pouring into Redisa. 69% of that money is spent on surplus, set up costs, Kusaga Taka, marketing and lobbying for the new waste stream from government. A mere 31% is actually spent on tyre related activities

LINK
As we delved deeper into the bowels of Redisa things got murkier and murkier. Hermann Erdmann has made no secret of the fact that he is angling for the government’s lucrative new waste stream project

Commentary 36
But alleges this source –the price is that Redisa must support SANCO

INSIDER 3
The deal is aimed at getting the second waste stream.

Commentary 37
Redisa has upgraded the civic organisations office, and documents suggest they will pay R18 million to salaries and expenses till June next year.
Redisa SAYS they are collaborating with SANCO TO MEET THE PLAN'S OBJECTIVES. They say they were required to process salaries on SANCO’s behalf until SANCO's payment system is developed, and all of this was independently audited. SANCO say it is not involved in the waste stream project, and BOTH SAY THEY HAVE a tightly controlled sponsorship agreement.

INSIDER 3
Sanco is very close to the government, and doing a deal with them, puts Redisa in the position to use that lever towards getting that second waste stream.

Commentary 38
Its tense right now at Redisa’s head office. The Staff are being forced to take polygraph tests. Sources say Hermann Erdman should be first in line. Meanwhile Redisa is churning out the good news PR. But in Mamelodi the waste pickers hope against odds they will get their money before Christmas.

THE END 18 17

In at 00 01 00 00
Out at 00 19 18 00
Duration 18 18

Promo one in at 00 19 30 00
Promo Two 00 20 00 00 00
Promo three 00 20 30 00 00
Plasma




PROMO ONE
In 2012 Redisa promised government they would create 10 000 jobs. How are they doing? Some say not well

Terence Sithole with a Redisa magazine
Here am I here! We look very happy, but in our pockets are we happy?


PROMO TWO
We follow the R2 30 per kilogram you pay every time you buy a tyre
Devi
Can we see Redisa’s books, can we see Kusaga Taka books?
Herman
No obviously not,
Why not?
Hermann
Because I don’t think it’s a reasonable request


PROMO THREE
Two years after we first met Redisa’s CEO, Herman Erdmann we go back to see how this tyre recycling and job creation plan is doing.

We look very happy, but in our pockets are we happy? Nothing! This is what we hoped for that we hoped for that we will grow. Commentary eighteen And the minister has bought the spin, hook, line and sinker But the minister is convinced that Redisa is delivering! Minister Edna Molewa Redisa has done well in ensuring jobs that are created, but also having taken away so many tyres away from the landfills LINK The whole point of the plan was to RECYCLE the tyres – but that part of the plan was barely working, tyres were piling up in the depots- Herman had to get rid of the tyres – and quickly Commentary nineteen So he turned to the solution favoured least in the plan. Burn the tyres for fuel in cement kilns. But the kilns were scattered all over South Africa, so Redisa spends millions on transport –money they should be spending on developing recyclers Devi Is every tyre recycled as we stand right now? Hermann It’s processed lets say that- ultimately we would like every tyre recycled not burnt Commentary Twenty But then the kilns filled up and could take no more tyres so Redisa started to export the tyres to India and Dubai -creating jobs overseas instead. Despite these leaked photos of baled tyres about to be shipped, Redisa say: they are not exporting tyres. REDISA delivers tyres to recyclers for processing and a percentage of shredded tyres are being exported. So they are exporting tyres! Source Shiva They could be burning most of the tyres, they could be exporting a lot, but those are all short-term solutions that can help you get your targets. Devi Ok Shiva The question from there is are you really creating a sustainable industry in SA and the answer is no Commentary Twenty- two Hermann has always maintained that tyre dumps attract mosquitoes, yet documents show Redisa was desperate to get rid of tyres, and approved 7000 tonnes to the Sunderland Shooting range after the range met the formal application requirements. Mosquito heaven- courtesy of Redisa! Devi Herman’s job is to collect the tyres that is what we are paying him for Source A But also remember the more you collect the more you need to pay out Commentary Twenty-Three Two years from now Redisa is mandated to deal with 100% of the tyres. Right now they only need to divert 50% of the tyres from landfills. But why spend millions simply diverting them from one place to another – last October Hermann admitted they had a problem Hermann And I tell you why we not collecting all the tyres yet – we don’t know where to put them Commentary Twenty- four One year later Redisa appears to have the same problem. These photos taken a few weeks ago show tyres at the Cape Depot piled high against the wall close to a power line. This is a violation of waste tyre storage regulations but Redisa say all their depots are fully compliant and they handled the Springs fire well Devi Ok so Herman is collecting the tyre tax levy but he doesn’t want to collect the tyres because what must he do with them? Source A It’s definitely not in Redisa’s interest to collect 100% of the tyres at this stage in time Commentary Twenty- five Albert Bothma had ticked all the boxes and his 51% BEE company become Redisa’s first approved recycler. Ask him if they have fulfilled their mandate and this is his response Albert That is so far from the truth at this point in time! Commentary Twenty-six To get the business off the ground all he needed was a guarantee from Redisa for 800 tonnes a month – and international investors would bring R150 million to the party – sulphur free diesel, waxes and electricity would have been made in this abandoned brewery. But he claims Redisa provided no such guarantee Albert It destroyed the project in the sense that the financiers said it doesn’t fall in their parameters any more Commentary Twenty- Seven Redisa say that Alberts plant is not in operation yet and they have commited to supplying an amount based on his current supply in his area. Albert just laughed when we read him their response. Redisa also says they are working with 11 new recyclers at various levels of activity Devi Link Then Herman went on a shopping Spree and spent millions on machinery, ostensibly to set up a few politically connected people in businesses Commentary Twenty-eight Redisa has denied that former special advisor to the minister Star Vilakazi will be a beneficiary of a tyre cutter – even though he has been listed as a beneficiary in this Redisa document. The other beneficiaries also have close political ties Source A In order to facilitate businesses for these individuals we were creating a industry that isn’t supposed to be there in between Redisa and the recyclers in other words – we are now putting an extra cost on this whole Redisa process just to help these guys make money Commentary Twenty-nine The plan says its crucial to identify likely candidates from MK, the Woman’s league and youth league and its those organisations who identify the individuals who benefit. Khotatso Moloi; Nafcoc secretary General Gilbert Mosena; Victor Molefe; Bafana Dube, and Tshepo Molai Devi to Herman Why did you want to help them? Herman It’s in the plan and we don’t do anything that is not in the plan Commentary thirty The machines are worth millions and we found them stored across the country. Victor Molefe is set up with R19.5 million worth of machinery Bafane Dube gets the R15.5 million moulding plant; ex MK Khotatso Moloi does well with R26 million rand’s worth of gear and a land cruiser and Gilbert Mosena even better with R29 million rand of equipment. They refused to comment but Tshepo Molai who has been named in the arms deal confirmed that he is negotiating a pre processing facility with Redisa. Devi There is no plan in this country where government doesn’t eat a big fat chunk of this how did you do this? Hermann laughs I maybe can quote what someone in the department said it was a politician. Redisa would be here, it doesn’t matter if somebody lobbies for it or not because it is the right thing to do Commentary thirty-one Small transporter Bongani Mkhabela had no idea that Redisa was looking for entrepreneurs close to the corridors of power –not down in the trenches where he was getting his hands dirty Bongani My journey with Redisa is something I would never wish anyone to be in – It’s only bought pain to me, my family and everyone else around me Commentary thirty-two He claims that when they took away his profitable route he suggested other opportunities within Redisa. Each time the answer was no – Redisa claims they have engaged Bongani on issues of non collection and there is an on going investigation Bongani Basically they shut me out of the business Devi What has happened to your truck? Bongani I had to sell it Devi And your house I lost my house as well …he breaks down Devi Are they happy? Hermann We have great feedback, in the beginning I said who are the people we are accountable to and I think it’s the waste pickers, the transporters and the recyclers because we are influencing their livelihood every day and we see them as our customers so we try to treat them like that Commentary thirty- three Bongani has no house but Hermann now has a selection. Redisa owns this R18 million rand mansion in Sandton, but this is Hermann’s primary address in Constantia, called Heaven of the Cape. It’s leased to a company- Westfalen owned by his wife and son. Westfalen has paid R1.74 million rand in advance for Hermann to live here. When we asked Redisa if any funds were paid to Westfalen they said no. But the next day they qualified this, saying that the property is also used for Redisa business and Westfalen does get R15 000 per month in lieue of business expenses Devi What would you like to say to people who insist that you are living the high life? Hermann I would like to talk about implementing the plan – it was something that we said if you have criticism in things we do come back to practical examples and become part of it Commentary 34 Well here is one example of many. Why did Redisa spend over R770 000 in a single month - June 2014 on travel and accommodation? Hermann is also a shareholder of the management company that administers Redisa. Its called Kusaga Taka Devi Can we see Redisa’s books, can we see Kusaga Taka books? Herman No obviously not, Why not? Hermann Because I don’t think it’s a reasonable request -we can’t go to Goodyear and say can we see your books! Commentary 35 From March to September over R327 million rand came pouring into Redisa. 69% of that money is spent on surplus, set up costs, Kusaga Taka, marketing and lobbying for the new waste stream from government. A mere 31% is actually spent on tyre related activities LINK As we delved deeper into the bowels of Redisa things got murkier and murkier. Hermann Erdmann has made no secret of the fact that he is angling for the government’s lucrative new waste stream project Commentary 36 But alleges this source –the price is that Redisa must support SANCO INSIDER 3 The deal is aimed at getting the second waste stream. Commentary 37 Redisa has upgraded the civic organisations office, and documents suggest they will pay R18 million to salaries and expenses till June next year. Redisa SAYS they are collaborating with SANCO TO MEET THE PLAN'S OBJECTIVES. They say they were required to process salaries on SANCO’s behalf until SANCO's payment system is developed, and all of this was independently audited. SANCO say it is not involved in the waste stream project, and BOTH SAY THEY HAVE a tightly controlled sponsorship agreement. INSIDER 3 Sanco is very close to the government, and doing a deal with them, puts Redisa in the position to use that lever towards getting that second waste stream. Commentary 38 Its tense right now at Redisa’s head office. The Staff are being forced to take polygraph tests. Sources say Hermann Erdman should be first in line. Meanwhile Redisa is churning out the good news PR. But in Mamelodi the waste pickers hope against odds they will get their money before Christmas. THE END 18 17 In at 00 01 00 00 Out at 00 19 18 00 Duration 18 18 Promo one in at 00 19 30 00 Promo Two 00 20 00 00 00 Promo three 00 20 30 00 00 Plasma PROMO ONE In 2012 Redisa promised government they would create 10 000 jobs. How are they doing? Some say not well Terence Sithole with a Redisa magazine Here am I here! We look very happy, but in our pockets are we happy? PROMO TWO We follow the R2 30 per kilogram you pay every time you buy a tyre Devi Can we see Redisa’s books, can we see Kusaga Taka books? Herman No obviously not, Why not? Hermann Because I don’t think it’s a reasonable request PROMO THREE Two years after we first met Redisa’s CEO, Herman Erdmann we go back to see how this tyre recycling and job creation plan is doing.
